Changing a password stores it as plain text, so `argon2.verify` can never match it at login. This is already recorded as lesson #88 in `LESSONS.md:8-16`, and the fix is still open in `CURRENT_FOCUS.md:13-14`. I traced the code to confirm it. I haven't run it against a database.

**The path**
1. `PUT /user` passes the raw body straight to the service (`src/user/user.controller.ts:26-29`). It has no validation pipe, unlike `POST /users` and `POST /users/login`.
2. `UserService.update()` runs `Object.assign(toUpdate, dto)` and saves (`src/user/user.service.ts:79-80`). A `password` field in the body is merged in unchanged. `UpdateUserDto` declares no `password`, but that's only a TypeScript type (`src/user/dto/update-user.dto.ts:1-6`) and removes nothing at runtime.
3. Hashing happens only in `UserEntity.hashPassword()`, which is `@BeforeInsert()` (`src/user/user.entity.ts:28-31`). There is no `@BeforeUpdate` on the user entity, and my grep found no other place that hashes a password. So the plain string goes into the `password` column.
4. At login, `argon2.verify(user.password, password)` (`src/user/user.service.ts:31`) is handed plain text where it expects a hash. It fails, `findOne` returns `null`, and the controller returns 401 (`src/user/user.controller.ts:48`).

The `delete toUpdate.password` at `user.service.ts:76` doesn't help. It only keeps the old hash when the body has no password. When a password is sent, `Object.assign` puts it back.

**To check on your side:** affected users should have a `password` value in the `user` table that doesn't start with `$argon2`. That would confirm the cause.

**Fix:** hash the password in `update()` when one is supplied. Also copy the allowed fields by name instead of merging the whole body (lesson #112). That also stops clients from setting `id` or other fields.

**Existing damage:** users already affected have plain text stored. Hashing on update won't repair them, so they'll need a password reset or a one-off migration that hashes those rows. A migration would run against your database, so I won't do it without your go-ahead.

Want me to make the fix in `update()`? Say whether you also want the whitelist change, or only hashing.
